territorial_scope.description: Amends a Latvian national statute; applies to the Latvian Ombudsman and its powers under Latvian law.

summary.short: Amends the Latvian Ombudsman Act so that the Ombudsman may request and access documentation of artificial intelligence systems needed in a case, and may ask the market surveillance authority to test an AI system with technical means if that documentation is insufficient. In force from 11 February 2026.
summary.long: The amending act changes the Latvian Ombudsman Act (Tiesībsarga likums). It adds two powers to Article 13: to request and access the documentation of artificial intelligence systems needed in a review case (point 15), and to ask the market surveillance authority, within its competence, to organise testing of an AI system with technical means where that documentation is insufficient (point 16). Article 27(1) is rewritten so that when the Ombudsman requests information under points 1, 1.1, 5, 13, 15 and 16 of Article 13, it sets the scope of that information and a reasonable time limit for providing it. The act also amends the informatory list of EU directives, removing points 1 and 4 and adding four directives on equal treatment, web and mobile accessibility, and work-life balance. The text sets no penalties, defines no AI system and specifies no numeric thresholds. The Saeima adopted it on 15 January 2026, the President promulgated it on 28 January 2026, and the publication metadata gives entry into force on 11 February 2026.

relations.note: Amending act: adds art. 13 points 15 and 16, replaces the first paragraph of art. 27, deletes points 1 and 4 and adds points 8 to 11 of the informative reference to EU directives.

notes: Amending act only: the base text of the Ombudsman law is not in the document, so amended provisions are known only as inserted or replaced wording. Sec. 3 deletes items 1 and 4 of the EU directive reference without naming them. Art. 27 cites point 1.1 of art. 13, which this act does not create. Point 16 refers to a market surveillance authority without naming it. The entry-into-force date (11.02.2026) appears only in the portal metadata, not in the act text; the act text gives adoption on 15 January 2026 and a signature date of 28 January 2026.

thresholds.note: The amending act contains no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment. Its numbers are article and point numbers (13. pants, 15. un 16. punkts, 27. panta pirmā daļa), directive numbers and years, and dates of adoption, promulgation and entry into force.
